key_insight: Carbon-tuned hBN-graphene alloys can sense multiple toxic gases through combined chemiresistive, work-function, and optical response changes, with different carbon contents favoring different analytes.
engineering_relevance: These alloys offer a promising low-cost platform for compact gas sensors for safety monitoring in medical, industrial, agricultural, and environmental applications.
method: Used first-principles density functional theory (DFT) to study gas adsorption on hBN-graphene alloys.
Screened Cl2, CO, CO2, NO, NO2, and HCN on alloys with different carbon fractions.
Evaluated adsorption energy, charge transfer, bandgap changes, work-function shifts, recovery time, and optical response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that BNGr-2 performed best for Cl2, CO, CO2, and HCN, BNGr-3 for NO and NO2, with ~20% work-function variation and recovery times on the order of 10^-1 to 10^-6 s.
watch_item: Results are computational and depend on idealized DFT models, so experimental validation under realistic operating conditions is still needed.
paper_title: First-Principles Investigation of Multimodal Toxic Gas Sensing in Carbon-Tuned hBN-Graphene Alloys: Chemiresistive, Work-Function, and Optical Responses
